_note: Frozen content for design review. Tools are the subject — one per page, set large, with what it replaced and what it costs.
brief: Five tools that replaced eight hundred a month of software

slots.titleItalic: Five tools now do what fourteen were doing badly, and the bill went from eight hundred a month to under fifty.

slots.bigStatement: It replaced three apps with one database and one place everyone actually looks.
slots.use1Body: Tasks, owners and deadlines in a view the whole team shares rather than four private lists.
slots.use2Body: Notes and decisions searchable instead of buried in a folder nobody opens.
slots.use3Body: Leads, notes and follow-ups in a pipeline that took an afternoon to build.

slots.bigStatement: It killed the file tool, the template library and every handoff argument in one move.
slots.use1Body: Deliverables shared with clean permissions and a link that does not expire.
slots.use2Body: Brand files, exports and backups in one place with actual version history.
slots.use3Body: No onboarding, no seat, no account for the client to create before they can look.

slots.bigStatement: It replaced copy tools, brainstorming calls and most of the drafting time.
slots.use1Body: Rough notes into a clear first version, which is the expensive part of writing.
slots.use2Body: Tone, structure and clarity without losing the way you actually sound.
slots.use3Body: Angles and outlines when you are stuck, which beats staring at the page.

slots.bigStatement: It replaced twenty open tabs and the guesswork that came with them.
slots.use1Body: A read on a market or a competitor in twenty minutes rather than an afternoon.
slots.use2Body: Every claim carries a link, so you can check the one that matters.
slots.use3Body: Options set side by side against criteria you chose, not a listicle.

slots.toolTagline: The meeting that did not happen
slots.bigStatement: It replaced status calls, long update threads and most of the calendar.
slots.use1Body: Three minutes recorded beats thirty minutes of five people listening.
slots.use2Body: Showing the screen removes the paragraph nobody was going to read anyway.
slots.use3Body: Comments land at the timestamp, so the context is never lost.

slots.bigStatement: Fewer tools means fewer places to hide, and one outage takes more with it.
slots.use1Body: When the one workspace is down, four jobs stop instead of one.
slots.use2Body: Anything you cannot get out in a usable format is not a tool, it is a landlord.
slots.use3Title: General beats specialist, until it does not
slots.use3Body: One app doing five jobs does each one about eighty per cent as well.

slots.body: Not all eleven. Pick the subscription you would not notice losing and let the gap tell you whether you actually needed it.
slots.signoff: The bill is the easy part to measure
